scope: Six Gulf/SEA routes; primary instrument and operational-owner stress tests. Four proposed follow-up designs, not institutional commitments. Existing model unchanged. Cutoff 2026-10-31; Geneva 2027-06-21/22. Source novelty and inherited evidence distinguished in companion markdown.

routes.headline: Supplier certification creates an entry point, but neither a seal nor independent assurance establishes a release veto

newEvidence.claim: FACT: The 20 January 2025 AI Seal announcement describes company certification and says government-project partners must be certified. Its listed assessment inputs concern activities, specialist employees, projects and partnerships, not a published system-level held-out failure threshold.
newEvidence.locator: Paragraphs beginning Companies that wish and All technology companies

newEvidence.claim: FACT, refreshed source/new comparison: The accelerator admits applications from all technology companies while prioritising Seal holders; entities enter at their readiness stage, including already-built services. Open application and mandatory partner certification refer to different stages and are not proven contradictory.
newEvidence.locator: Overview; Apply: AI Companies; final Government Entities section

supports: INFERENCE: A service owner can be selected before rebuilding a whole programme; joining an already-built service may shorten the experimental path.
INFERENCE: Company qualification and service acceptance provide distinct points at which to demand evidence.
challenges: INFERENCE: Neither accreditation of a company nor cybersecurity expertise establishes independence from the delivery team, access to failure logs, or authority to stop production.
INFERENCE: Procurement entry restrictions can disadvantage young SMEs without improving the safety of a particular agent; assess this separately from testing quality.

INFERENCE: A local service owner may control tool permissions and acceptance even when a foreign model provider will not negotiate model-level terms. This confines reach to the service rather than the global model.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED AFTER BOUNDED SEARCH: named independent assurer, independence/conflict policy, signed acceptance schedule and actual held release.
UNDISCLOSED IN READ PROGRAMME PAGE: cohort service IDs, actual readiness/review costs and dated deployment decisions; not a claim that these are legally confidential.
FUTURE: before-Geneva test results and public-service harm reduction.
routes.decisionTest: Before counting adoption, produce one service-specific acceptance instrument naming the person who can deny action permissions, an assessor outside the build team, and a witnessed failed-test hold. Falsified if the same failing version can be released by programme sponsorship alone.

ideas.title: Action-permission acceptance, independent of supplier badge
ideas.proposal: PROPOSAL: Start with one existing service ready for deployment. Bind each consequential tool action to an acceptance manifest covering model version, retrieval data, tool scopes and rollback version; retain an assisted-human route.
ideas.owner: Selected government service owner and its authorised release/procurement decision-maker; DCAI coordinates; Digital Dubai/DESC supply relevant review capability. Exact delegation and assessor still to be established.
ideas.mechanism: Service acceptance schedule plus production tool-credential provisioning; change control invalidates acceptance after material model/tool changes.
ideas.safetyDemand: No unauthorised filing, disclosure or irreversible action; no silent deprivation of service when the agent is stopped.
ideas.verification: Independent team holds back adversarial Arabic/English documents and malformed requests; plant one known critical failure. Record whether production credentials stay disabled, then test fresh variants after repair. Compare assisted completion, erroneous submissions, waiting time and subgroup failures against the current manual channel.
ideas.remedy: Withhold only the failing action capability, route cases to staff, restore prior approved version and require fresh retest; payment hold only if the actual contract authorises it.
ideas.deadline: Proposed: owner/instrument by 2027-01-31; first failure drill by 2027-03-31; held-out retest and service continuity results by 2027-06-01.
ideas.dependencies: Owner delegation; supplier version/configuration access; independent assessor capacity; data permissions; staffed fallback.
ideas.whyBetter: Tests a controllable local boundary and service-user outcomes without pretending Seal status verifies every deployment or assuming bargaining power over the foundation-model provider.

scoreImplications.implication: Keep conditional; no automatic upgrade from Seal
scoreImplications.reason: Company eligibility is a different object from system acceptance.

scoreImplications.implication: Retain unknown for full deployment; investigate already-built entry route
scoreImplications.reason: Flexible entry exists but no observed review duration is disclosed.
Independent assurance wording supplies no demonstrated binding stop.

routes.headline: Real CST deployment history does not establish an AI stop-rule; SDAIA offers a stronger adjacent case-selection pool

newEvidence.claim: PARTICIPANT REPORT: Myriota reports graduating from CST and deploying remote smart water meters with CST, stc and Giza Systems for the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture. It describes full commercial service as the next step. This is a named implementation, not an AI safety test or proof that graduation itself authorises full rollout.
newEvidence.locator: Post body, paragraphs on deployment and next stop

newEvidence.claim: FACT ABOUT OFFICIAL REGISTER: SDAIA's separate data sandbox lists six named 2025-cohort graduates, including AI legal service Hojjah, Arabic medical-transcription provider Sahl AI and Waki children's biometric payments. Entries distinguish joining in Rabi al-Awwal 1447 and graduation in Shawwal 1447. No exact Gregorian day is inferred.
newEvidence.locator: Graduate list: Codata, Hojjah, Medical Circles, Sahl AI, Smart Reach, Waki

newEvidence.claim: FACT: SDAIA lists October 2026 opening for its personal-data track, January 2027 for data monetisation, and post-exit monitoring. The header says 60-day service duration, but the FAQ makes participation duration dependent on the approved plan. Neither establishes a 60-day completed AI test.
newEvidence.locator: Main tracks; participant journey stages 3–7; FAQ duration and post-exit monitoring

supports: INFERENCE: Myriota identifies an actual end customer and integrators, narrowing the operational-owner search beyond cohort logos.
INFERENCE: SDAIA's named AI graduates create a testable post-exit follow-up pool with higher case specificity than CST mixed-technology totals.
challenges: FACT/BOUNDARY: SDAIA and CST are separate programmes. SDAIA graduations, terms and dates cannot be credited to the CST route.
INFERENCE: Completing compliance requirements does not show a previously unsafe action was blocked. The six graduated entries are a selected set, not a pass rate.
INFERENCE: A stopped health or school payment service can itself harm users; fallback must be assessed alongside privacy containment.
INFERENCE: The relevant school/hospital/customer controls service access; a technology regulator alone may not hold all operational switches.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED AFTER SEARCH: CST participant-level AI failures, corrective notices, signed test plans and full-rollout authorisations.
UNDISCLOSED IN READ SDAIA REGISTER: failed/withdrawn applications, incident logs, underlying acceptance criteria, assessor independence and user volumes.
UNSEARCHED: complete individual customer contracts for all six SDAIA graduates; no institutional consent inferred.
FUTURE: January 2027 monetisation track and proposed retest outcomes.
routes.decisionTest: Obtain a specific CST AI participant plan and customer release authority. If unavailable, investigate SDAIA as an explicitly separate route, not a silent replacement. Falsifier: neither regulator nor service owner can impose or observe an operational restriction after a critical failure.

ideas.title: Post-graduation drift and fallback audit
ideas.proposal: PROPOSAL, adjacent SDAIA route: choose Waki or Sahl AI from the published graduate list; test whether post-exit monitoring can catch a changed model or configuration and cause customer-level restriction.
ideas.owner: SDAIA data-sandbox programme, chosen provider, and the actual school/payment or hospital service owner; sector regulator if applicable.
ideas.mechanism: Post-exit monitoring plan plus customer configuration/change-control agreement, explicitly separate from CST admission.
ideas.safetyDemand: For Waki, prevent cross-child account association and unauthorised biometric retention while maintaining non-biometric access to purchases. For Sahl AI, prevent wrong-patient attribution and require clinical confirmation of consequential transcript fields.
ideas.verification: Choose only one use case. Use authorised synthetic identities and independently held-out variants; seed a controlled configuration regression; inspect timestamped alert, restriction, fallback and retest. Falsified if graduation badge substitutes for new evidence or safe fallback cannot serve users.
ideas.remedy: Disable affected biometric/AI feature, retain card/QR or clinician-mediated service, correct affected records, verify deletion where required, and re-enable only after fresh tests.
ideas.deadline: Proposed: select owner and approved monitoring scope by 2027-01-15; drill by 2027-03-15; post-change retest by 2027-06-01.
ideas.dependencies: Graduate/customer consent, applicable sector permissions, version logs, non-biometric/manual channel, SDAIA confirmation that the proposed follow-up is within its programme.
ideas.whyBetter: Uses named graduated AI services and an explicit post-exit stage; directly tests lasting control rather than counting graduation certificates.

scoreImplications.implication: Do not transfer adjacent-programme maturity to CST
scoreImplications.reason: Actual SDAIA AI cases improve alternative selection, not evidence of CST's exact safeguard.
Service duration and plan-specific participation duration are explicitly different.
Post-exit monitoring is published but a restriction and corrective retest are not demonstrated.

routes.headline: MORADA supplies a concrete internal submission gate, but its automated rejection is a price check, not an AI safety hold

newEvidence.claim: OFFICIAL OPERATIONAL REPORT: On 8 June 2026 Pusdatin introduced MORADA in KATALISTIK. MORADA SSI uses AI to extract project plans into work specifications and requires an EGA SPBE clearance letter for DIPA-funded requests. MORADA APD automatically rejects hardware requests exceeding prescribed price limits.
newEvidence.locator: Opening and bullet points Morada SSI / Morada APD

newEvidence.claim: OFFICIAL INTENT, NOT VERIFIED COMPLIANCE: The closing paragraph aims to end ICT service/procurement submissions outside the integrated system. It does not prove all units comply or that software release is impossible outside MORADA.

supports: INFERENCE: Pusdatin now has a named, AI-using workflow and documented submission requirements; a pilot can attach to an existing service rather than wait for a general PDP rollout.
INFERENCE: The same platform can potentially preserve request, evidence and rejection timestamps.
challenges: INFERENCE: An AI-generated work specification can introduce procurement errors before any public-facing licensing AI is deployed. This is a different threat surface from the previously selected marketing-authorisation system.
INFERENCE: Automatic hardware-price rejection proves only a narrow rule implementation. It does not establish DPIA or production-release authority.
SOURCE QUALITY: The page's March ticket headline says 1,488, while its 765 requests plus 773 incidents sum to 1,538; do not use that inconsistent denominator for capacity or effectiveness.
INFERENCE: Buying units, budget/clearance authorities and production owners remain separate dependencies; a 0.75 coordination score should not be justified solely by being within one agency.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED: signed delegation, actual MORADA rejection/override logs, applicable project template and release acceptance.
UNRESOLVED IN PRIOR PASS, NOT RE-VERIFIED HERE: full PP 33/2026 and its relationship to the selected gate.
UNDISCLOSED IN READ ARTICLE: provider/model, processing data categories, number of AI-extracted specifications and error rate.
FUTURE: authorised injected-document and correction experiment.
routes.decisionTest: Can the authorised Pusdatin/buying-unit workflow owner reject or correct an AI-extracted specification before it becomes an approved procurement input? A planted missing clearance or materially altered specification must fail closed; retain the original source document and authorised correction.

ideas.title: Source-to-specification integrity gate in MORADA
ideas.proposal: PROPOSAL: Pilot at MORADA SSI, explicitly a narrower variant of the BPOM route. Require provenance links from every critical generated requirement to its approved project-plan passage and a machine-checkable clearance identifier.
ideas.owner: Head of BPOM Pusdatin and the authorised SSI request reviewer, with the buying unit and EGA SPBE clearance authority confirming their respective decisions.
ideas.mechanism: Existing project-submission validation and authorised reviewer sign-off before generated specifications become procurement inputs; permissions and override logging.
ideas.safetyDemand: No silent change to cost, data-access, evaluation or security requirements; no fabricated or omitted clearance.
ideas.verification: Blindly mix clean documents with synthetic conflicting annexes and instruction-like text. Independent reviewer compares approved source to generated/accepted specification. Preserve failed submission, correction and fresh-document retest; measure false holds and review workload against manual extraction.
ideas.remedy: Reject generated specification, use manual source-based review, repair extraction/configuration and retest; do not automatically cancel the underlying legitimate service request.
ideas.deadline: Proposed: authorisation and template by 2027-01-31; failure/correction exercise by 2027-03-31; workload and held-out retest by 2027-06-01.
ideas.dependencies: Actual template and delegation, authorised synthetic corpus, access to validation/override history, confirmation that selected documents contain relevant personal data before calling it a DPIA demonstration.
ideas.whyBetter: Targets a demonstrably AI-using internal workflow with a concrete acceptance boundary. It can expose unsafe procurement requirements early without claiming broader licensing coverage.

scoreImplications.implication: Qualitative upgrade for a narrowed internal-workflow pilot
scoreImplications.reason: Actual named platform, input requirements and validation function replace an abstract institutional analogy.
No matched specification/request denominator; this is not the licensing-system population.
Pusdatin, buying unit and clearance authority perform different decisions.

routes.headline: Existing ADMP guidance is more specific than generic DPIA thresholds; a real consultation submission exposes supplier-bargaining and human-oversight gaps

newEvidence.claim: FACT: ADMP guideline section 6.1 treats ADMP as a qualitative DPIA trigger regardless of intended extent. Section 1.3 calls for earliest-stage DPO engagement. Section 10.2.6 says AI must not be the sole factor, but it sits under 10.2's formulation that the controller may adopt the following best practices. Do not flatten this wording into a separately enforced statutory AI ban.

STAKEHOLDER POSITION: Edwin Lee & Partners reports filing on 22 October 2026 and argues the draft framework is softer/inconsistent with ADMP guidance. It proposes explicit status, capable human oversight, proportionate records and recognition that most buyers accept global supplier standard terms.
newEvidence.locator: Legal effect; Buying AI; ADMP and human oversight; One record, one assessment

newEvidence.claim: FACT ABOUT A PROPOSED INSTRUMENT: The firm's Annex C distinguishes a standard-terms/settings checklist from negotiable model clauses. Clauses 3,6–8 address settings changes, incident information including model/version, deletion and audit. Bracketed periods and clauses are proposals, not executed contracts or regulator-adopted requirements.
newEvidence.locator: PDF pp.1–5, especially model clauses 3 and 6–8

supports: INFERENCE: A commercial ADMP deployment can be selected using functional risk rather than large data-subject thresholds alone.
INFERENCE: The actual submitted contract checklist makes the standard-form versus negotiated-purchase distinction operational.
challenges: INFERENCE: A compulsory novel supplier covenant may be least feasible for SMEs. A local permission/configuration gate can sometimes be implemented without obtaining global-provider agreement.
INFERENCE: Human review is ineffective if staff cannot inspect evidence, overturn decisions or meet workload demands.
BOUNDARY: A lawyer's submission is a viewpoint and proposed drafting; it supplies neither legal adoption nor representative SME consent.
INFERENCE: Privacy documentation can miss wrong decisions, discriminatory errors or unsafe advice; link the DPIA to an actual service outcome and correction.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED: named commercial controller with executed AI-specific acceptance terms, dated DPIA and failed-test hold.
UNDISCLOSED IN READ DOCUMENTS: observed enforcement of section 10.2.6, reviewer capacity, provider acceptance of Annex C.
FUTURE: final AI framework text and any new implementation transition; the submitted 12-month transition is not adopted law.
routes.decisionTest: Select an actual AI-assisted eligibility or claims workflow and show that a qualified reviewer can override it, a material settings change triggers review, and affected users obtain correction. Falsified if review merely rubber-stamps outputs or the controller cannot restrict data/tools after a supplier change.

ideas.title: Proportionate controller-owned configuration and correction gate
ideas.proposal: PROPOSAL: One controller-owned AI processing/acceptance record combines applicable DPIA, exact provider terms, service settings, model/version, test results and a corrective-action register. Use standard terms honestly; negotiate added clauses only where the controller can do so.
ideas.owner: Selected commercial controller's senior responsible manager, DPO and service operations owner; independent test reviewer; vendor assistance where contractually available.
ideas.mechanism: Controller's approval of data access and consequential-action permissions, configuration-change trigger and human appeal/correction workflow, attached to the actual DPIA.
ideas.safetyDemand: No unreviewable adverse decision; no training/data-sharing configuration outside the approved purpose; meaningful human override and timely correction.
ideas.verification: Held-out paired cases include correct and erroneous AI recommendations; reviewers must detect and overturn planted critical errors without knowing which are planted. Test supplier settings drift and data-retrieval/correction on synthetic records. Track harmful accepted errors, false holds, appeal reversals, time and workload by affected group. Falsified by identical adverse decisions despite corrected source evidence or by unavailable corrective access.
ideas.remedy: Disable the affected feature/data feed, revert to assisted processing, correct the person's record/decision, and require fresh independent retest before restoring permissions.
ideas.deadline: Proposed: controller and acceptance record by 2027-01-31; first oversight/configuration drill by 2027-03-31; fresh retest and correction outcomes by 2027-06-01.
ideas.dependencies: Actual controller selection; applicable legal scope; provider settings/log access; skilled reviewers; staffed correction channel; justified data retention.
ideas.whyBetter: Reduces duplicated paperwork and avoids assuming SME bargaining power. Tests substantive correction and capability control instead of DPIA completion alone. Could inform a separately authorised Thai or Vietnamese public-service test without transferring Malaysian law.

scoreImplications.implication: More specific eligibility evidence, not demonstrated adoption
scoreImplications.reason: ADMP is an explicit qualitative trigger but no chosen controller has implemented the proposed gate.
The actor who controls local use need not control upstream supplier contract terms.

scoreImplications.implication: Do not upgrade from best-practice wording
scoreImplications.reason: A hold and corrective retest remain unobserved; contextual wording matters.

routes.headline: AIGPC has an actual contracted operator, but the recovered contract purchases capacity-building rather than operational AI safety gates

newEvidence.claim: FACT: ETDA's December 2025 contract register identifies AIGPC establishment/management project 68119464442, supplier Bolliger & Company (Thailand), contract CO68120010 dated 22 December 2025, THB 13,240,180. Status records contract/PO made, not completed performance. Award notice is dated 17 December 2025.

newEvidence.claim: FACT: Published tender/TOR specifies completion by 31 August 2026 and four payment stages of 20/30/35/15 percent conditional on ETDA acceptance. Deliverables include governance courses, publications, meetings and a conference. Learner pre/post-tests are not model-safety tests.
newEvidence.locator: PDF pp.23–29; TOR 4.3–4.7 and 7–9; tender p.16

newEvidence.claim: INFERENCE FROM INSTRUMENT: Sandbox appears in the centre's general R&D description, but the recovered contracted deliverables do not establish participant-specific admission, release veto, independent adversarial testing or corrective deployment action. The historical contract cannot prove the announced 2027 sandbox has these powers.
newEvidence.locator: PDF p.19 background versus TOR deliverables pp.20–29

supports: INFERENCE: Programme maturity should not be dismissed as a new October announcement: an identified operator and actual procurement commitment predate it.
INFERENCE: ETDA's acceptance committee is a concrete owner of purchased deliverables, distinct from the owner of a participant's production service.
challenges: INFERENCE: Counting contract value, conference participation or learner tests as safety-gated deployment exaggerates reach and remedy.

INFERENCE: Published August 2026 completion is already past at cutoff; any new June 2027 intervention needs the succeeding work order or another lawful instrument, not assumed spare authority in this contract.
INFERENCE: Combining adoption support and independent assurance in the same contractor creates a potential conflict that must be examined, not assumed disqualifying or solved.
INFERENCE: A small public-service experiment could be faster than full sandbox graduation; non-AI DSS durations are weak evidence against that narrower design.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED: acceptance certificate/payment for this contract, amended expiry or FY2027 work order, and live AI sandbox participant contract.
UNDISCLOSED IN READ INSTRUMENT: evaluator conflict rules and operational hold authority.
UNSEARCHED: complete contract register for every 2026 month; no claim that no successor exists.

Require a paid deliverable consisting of a witnessed failure, owner-imposed restriction, repair and fresh test. scoreImplications.reason: Named signed-contract record materially improves institutional specificity.

routes.headline: The legal route remains plausible, but the kiosk candidate may be assistance rather than a qualifying decisional system

newEvidence.claim: REFRESHED OFFICIAL REPORT / NEW FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS: Dong Tien's kiosk integrates conversational assistance, speech, OCR, VNeID and online services; the supplier is Tan Thanh Phuong. The description supports preparation/submission assistance and planned expansion, not a finding that the kiosk itself issues administrative decisions.
newEvidence.locator: Opening; service journey paragraph; supplier paragraph; concluding conditional expansion

newEvidence.claim: REFRESHED OFFICIAL REPORT / ALTERNATIVE LEAD: The Thanh Hoa implementation article also identifies operational AI vehicle recognition, electronic weighing and real-time mineral-extraction monitoring connected to authorities. It offers a potentially more consequential workflow to classify, but no named mine contract, AI02 or enforcement decision.
newEvidence.locator: Section Dua AI vao giai quyet cac bai toan cua dia phuong, mineral-management paragraphs

supports: INFERENCE: A named kiosk supplier and specific interfaces make a local test technically definable.
INFERENCE: Existing mineral-monitoring workflows may provide an alternative where AI outputs influence enforcement, if that actual decisional use can be established.
challenges: INFERENCE: Wrong procedural advice may still harm citizens, but harm potential does not automatically establish Article 20 or high-risk catalogue eligibility.
INFERENCE: A five-official service centre may struggle with an added review queue; an AI stop must preserve accessible manual service.
INFERENCE: VNeID and online-service dependencies mean the kiosk vendor alone cannot necessarily implement all access/correction changes.
INFERENCE: The strongest legal deadline is useless as a feasibility advantage if the chosen system is outside its scope or no authorised actor implements the required restriction.
unknowns: NOT RECOVERED AFTER BOUNDED SEARCH: underlying Thanh Hoa plan 129/KH-UBND; no new signed local instrument recovered in this pass.
NOT LOCATED: completed AI02, kiosk acceptance contract, delegation, changed decisions and measured affected users.
UNSEARCHED: individual mineral-site procurement/inspection files; alternative lead only.
INHERITED, NOT NEWLY VERIFIED HERE: Decree 142 Article 20 and Decision 33 transition dates from prior evidence ledger; these still require case-specific applicability.
FUTURE: proposed restriction, service continuity and corrective retest before Geneva.
routes.decisionTest: First trace one AI output into an actual administrative decision and establish the statutory scope and signatory. If it is only assistance, honestly run a voluntary service-owner quality/safety test instead of claiming a statutory AI02 gate. Falsifier for the statutory route: no qualifying decision link, no applicable assessment duty, or no authorised restriction.

scoreImplications.implication: Challenge the one-signature equals one-owner shortcut
scoreImplications.reason: Supplier, identity integration, online public service and frontline operations have distinct roles.
